name: cleanup
description: Clean the comments in a diff range or path. Deletes narration, history and commented-out code, shortens the rest, keeps every why, trap and coupling. Never changes code behaviour. Use when asked to clean, trim or fix comments.
argument-hint: "[range | path ...]"
allowed-tools: Bash(git diff *), Bash(git status *), Bash(python3 *), Bash(python *)

# Cleanup

Scope: `$ARGUMENTS`. A git range (`main..HEAD`) means only the comments the
range ADDED. A path means every comment in those files. With no argument,
use the working tree and staged changes (`git diff HEAD`); if that is empty,
ask which files.

## Steps

1. Mechanical pass first. Run
   `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check_comments.py" --diff-file -`
   with the diff on stdin (or `python` if `python3` is missing). For a path,
   run it with `--file <path>`; for a git range, pass the range directly.
2. Read each comment in scope and sort it into one bucket:
   - **delete**: narration of what the code does, history (`previously`,
     `changed from`, `fixed`, `now we`, `new:`), commented-out code, a bare
     issue ref, a docblock that only restates the signature.
   - **shorten**: it holds a real why, trap or coupling but takes more than
     two sentences or wraps it in filler. Rewrite to one or two plain sentences.
   - **keep**: a why, a trap, a hidden coupling, a licence header, a tool
     directive with a reason, a TODO with a concrete condition, a short API doc.
   - **unsure**: you cannot tell whether it hides a why. Do not touch it.
3. Apply only the delete and shorten buckets. Edit comment text only.
   Never touch a code token, a string, or a blank line that separates code.
   When a deleted comment leaves an empty line that was not there before,
   remove it.
4. Verify: `git diff -U0` the files you touched. Every removed line and every
   added line must be a comment line. If any code line changed, revert that
   hunk.
5. Report in this shape:

```
cleanup: N deleted, M shortened, K kept, U unsure
unsure (left as is):
- path:line  "<comment>"  because <one clause>
```

# Comments

Clear code needs no comment. Before writing one, ask: can the code say this
instead? Rename, extract, or simplify first. If the comment still earns its
place, it is one of three kinds:

| Kind | It answers | Example |
|---|---|---|
| WHY | a reason or constraint the code cannot show | `// 300ms: the API rejects more than 3 calls per second.` |
| TRAP | an order that matters, a platform quirk, a workaround and its cause | `# Flush before fork: the child inherits the buffer.` |
| HIDDEN COUPLING | changing this breaks something elsewhere; name it | `-- Keep in sync with STATUS in api/status.go.` |

One or two short plain sentences. If the comment is harder to read than the
code, delete it.

## Banned

- Narration of what the lines do: `// loop over users and add to list`.
- History of how the code got here: `// changed from X`, `// previously`,
  `// fixed bug where`, `// now we`, `// new:`. That is the commit message.
- An issue number as the whole comment: `// #1234`, `// PROJ-12`.
  Say the why; the ticket may follow it.
- Commented-out code. Delete it. Git remembers.
- Docblocks that restate the signature: `/** Gets the user. @param id the id */`.

## Allowed and wanted

- Public API docs where the language's tooling reads them (docstrings,
  `///`, `/** */`), kept short: what it does, what it returns, what it
  raises. Nothing the signature already says.
- Licence headers.
- Tool directives with a reason: `# noqa: E501  URL cannot wrap`,
  `// eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- CLI entry point`.
- TODOs that name a concrete condition: `// TODO: drop when Node 18 is out of support.`

## Examples

Python
```python
# bad: narration and history
# loop over the orders and sum the totals
# previously used reduce
total = sum(o.total for o in orders)

# good: nothing. The line says it.
total = sum(o.total for o in orders)

# good: a trap
time.sleep(0.2)  # The API rate-limits bursts under 200ms apart.
```

TypeScript
```ts
// bad: restates the signature
/** Parses a date string and returns a Date. @param s the string */
export function parseDate(s: string): Date {

// good: a trap
export function parseDate(s: string): Date {
  // Safari rejects "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"; the T separator is required.
  return new Date(s.replace(" ", "T"));
}
```

C#
```cs
// bad: history
// Fixed bug where the token was refreshed twice. Now we check expiry first.
if (_cache.TryGet(out var t) && !Expired(t)) return t;

// good: nothing. The condition says it.
if (_cache.TryGet(out var t) && !Expired(t)) return t;

// good: a why
using var stream = File.Open(path, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read, FileShare.Read);
// Windows keeps the lock until dispose; readers in other processes need Read share.
```

Go
```go
// bad: narration
// open the file with the flags
f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE|os.O_SYNC, 0o600)

// good: a why
// O_SYNC: the WAL relies on each write hitting disk before the ack.
f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE|os.O_SYNC, 0o600)
```

SQL
```sql
-- bad: commented-out code and a bare ticket
-- SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE status IS NULL;
-- PROJ-881
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status ON orders(status) WHERE status IS NOT NULL;

-- good: a why
-- Partial index: 90% of rows have status NULL and are never queried.
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status ON orders(status) WHERE status IS NOT NULL;
```

## When reviewing

A narrative comment is a WARNING, never a blocker. Put all of them in one
finding, raised once per branch, and never raise it again in a later round,
fixed or not. Never flag a comment the change did not touch.

# Install commentie into this project

Ask before every change, one question at a time. Show the exact text or
diff first.

## 1. Project rule

Find `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` at the project root. If both exist, prefer
`CLAUDE.md`. If neither exists, ask which to create. Skip this step when the
file already contains a `## Comments` heading.

Propose appending:

```md
## Comments

Follow the `commentie:comments` skill. Clear code needs no comment. Comment only
a non-obvious why, a trap, or a hidden coupling, in one or two short sentences.
No narration, no history, no commented-out code, no bare issue refs.
Reviewers: a narrative comment is a warning, reported once per branch, never a blocker.
```

## 2. Script wiring (optional)

Before asking, tell the user what the script is, in two or three lines:
`check_comments.py` is a regex check, not a model. It reads only the added
lines of a diff and flags history words, bare issue refs, commented-out code
and long blocks. It costs no tokens, finishes in under a second, gives the
same result every run, and covers commits from people who do not use Claude.
With `--strict` it can fail the commit or the job, which an AI review usually
cannot. It is worth adding when the project has no AI review, wants a hard
gate, or already uses pre-commit. If CI already runs an AI review that reads
the comments rule and warnings are enough, say the script is optional and
skipping it is fine.

The plugin path changes on every update, so a pre-commit hook or CI step
should not point into it. Offer to copy
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check_comments.py` to `scripts/check_comments.py`
in the project (one stdlib file, no dependencies). Only then offer, each as
its own question:

- **pre-commit**: if `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists, add
  ```yaml
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: commentie
        name: commentie
        entry: python scripts/check_comments.py --staged
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
  ```
  If `package.json` has husky or lint-staged, add
  `python scripts/check_comments.py --staged` to the pre-commit script.
  Otherwise offer a plain `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and say it is local only.
- **CI**: if `.github/workflows/` exists, add a step to the main workflow:
  ```yaml
  - run: python scripts/check_comments.py origin/${{ github.base_ref || 'main' }}..HEAD
  ```
  with `fetch-depth: 0` on the checkout.

Default to warning-only (no `--strict`). Mention `--strict` once as the
opt-in that fails the commit or the job.

## 3. Hook

Say in one line: the after-edit check is off; enable it with
`/plugin configure commentie@devkit` and turn on "Check comments after each edit".

Finish with a two-line summary of what changed.

# commentie

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/commentie.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/commentie)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/commentie.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/commentie)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/commentie.svg)](https://github.com/mfozmen/commentie/blob/main/LICENSE)

A Claude Code and OpenCode plugin that keeps code comments few, short and
plain.

AI-written code fills with narrative comments, and reviews then loop on fixing
prose. commentie teaches the rule while code is written, cleans up on demand,
and guards cheaply: a stdlib script first, a cheap read-only critic second, and
the critic warns once per branch and never blocks.

## The rule

Clear code needs no comment. Comment only what the code cannot say: a
non-obvious **why**, a **trap**, or a **hidden coupling**. One or two short
sentences. Banned: narration, history, bare issue refs, commented-out code,
docblocks that restate the signature.

## What you get

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| Rule | The writing rule, with examples in Python, TypeScript, C#, Go and SQL. |
| Cleanup | Deletes narration and history, shortens the rest, keeps every why, trap and coupling. Never touches code. Lists what it was unsure about instead of deleting it. |
| Critic | Read-only review of the comments a diff range added. One WARNING finding, raised once per branch. |
| Script | Stdlib, no dependencies. Flags history words, bare issue refs, commented-out code and long blocks in the added lines of a diff. |
| Hook | Off by default. Runs the script after an edit and shows findings as a warning. Never blocks. |
| Install | Adds the rule to CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md and offers pre-commit or CI wiring. Asks before every change. |

## Claude Code

```
/plugin marketplace add mfozmen/devkit
/plugin install commentie@devkit
```

- Rule: the `commentie:comments` skill, loaded when Claude edits code.
- Cleanup: `/commentie:cleanup [range | path]`.
- Install: `/commentie:install`.
- Critic: the read-only `commentie:comment-critic` agent, on Haiku.

The after-edit hook is off by default. Enable it with
`/plugin configure commentie@devkit` and turn on "Check comments after each
edit", or at install time:

```
claude plugin install commentie@devkit --config hook_enabled=true
```

## OpenCode

For a local checkout, point the config at the repo directory:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["file:///absolute/path/to/commentie"]
}
```

Once published to npm, `"plugin": ["commentie"]` works too. The plugin
registers itself; no files are copied into the project.

- Rule: the same rule, injected into the system prompt.
- Cleanup: `/commentie-cleanup [range | path]`.
- Install: `/commentie-install`.
- Critic: the read-only `comment-critic` subagent, using your default model
  unless pinned.

The after-edit hook is off by default. Add options as the second element of the
plugin entry:

```json
{
  "plugin": [["file:///absolute/path/to/commentie", { "hook": true }]]
}
```

- `hook` (default `false`): append findings to the tool result after an edit.
- `criticModel`: pin the critic to a model, for example
  `"anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"`.

`COMMENTIE_HOOK=true` enables the hook too. The hook finds `python3` or `python`
on `PATH`.

## The script

```
python scripts/check_comments.py                 # staged changes
python scripts/check_comments.py main..HEAD      # a range
python scripts/check_comments.py --file src/a.py # one file against HEAD
python scripts/check_comments.py --strict ...    # exit 1 on findings
python scripts/check_comments.py --self-test
```

Output is `file:line: reason`. Exit code is 0 unless `--strict`.
Skip patterns with a `.commentie-allow` file at the repo root, one regex per
line. Change the long-block threshold with `--max-block N` (default 5).

## Evals

```
python scripts/check_comments.py --self-test
python evals/run_evals.py
```

`evals/fixtures` holds diffs labelled narrative or useful, with the expected
script findings and critic verdict in `evals/expected.json`. The useful set is
real why, trap and coupling comments the script must not flag. Critic verdicts
are checked by running `@agent-commentie:comment-critic` on a fixture applied
to a scratch repo.

## Releasing

Releases are cut by [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please)
from [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). PRs are
squash-merged, so the PR title is the commit: `feat: ...` bumps the minor
version, `fix: ...` the patch, `feat!: ...` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer the
minor while below 1.0. `docs`, `ci`, `chore`, `test` and `refactor` release
nothing on their own. After each merge to `main`, release-please updates a
release PR that bumps `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `package.json` and
`CHANGELOG.md`; merging it tags `vX.Y.Z` and publishes the GitHub release.
Publishing the same version to npm with `npm publish` makes
`"plugin": ["commentie"]` work for OpenCode; a local path works without it.

name: comment-critic
description: Read-only review of the comments ADDED in a diff range. Use during code review or before opening a PR. Reports narrative comments as one warning-level finding, raised once per branch, never a blocker. Pass the range, e.g. "main..HEAD"; defaults to the default branch..HEAD.
model: claude-haiku-5-5
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
disallowedTools: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit
maxTurns: 15
color: yellow
---

You review only the comments a change adds. You never edit files.

## The rule

Clear code needs no comment. A comment earns its place only as:
- a non-obvious WHY (a reason or a constraint),
- a TRAP (an order that matters, a platform quirk, a workaround and its cause),
- a HIDDEN COUPLING (changing this breaks something elsewhere, named).

One or two short plain sentences. Banned: narration of what the lines do,
history of how the code got here, bare issue refs, commented-out code,
docblocks that restate the signature.

Allowed, do not flag: short public API docs, licence headers, tool directives
with a reason, TODOs that name a concrete condition.

## Procedure

1. Range. Use the range from your prompt. Otherwise find the default branch
   with `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` (fall back to `main`) and
   use `<default>..HEAD`. If HEAD is the default branch, use `--cached` plus
   the working tree (`git diff HEAD`).
2. Mechanical pass. Run
   `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check_comments.py" <range>`
   (or `python` if `python3` is missing). Take its findings and its line
   numbers as given; they come from the diff. Do not recount.
3. Added lines only. Run `git diff -U0 <range>` and judge every ADDED comment
   against the rule. Ignore removed and context lines completely: a comment
   the change did not touch is never your business.
4. Once per branch. Read `.git/commentie/<branch>` (branch name with `/`
   replaced by `-`) if it exists. Each line is `path<TAB>normalized comment
   text`. Drop every candidate whose path and text already appear there,
   fixed or not. After reporting, append your new candidates to that file
   (create the directory if needed). This file is the only thing you write.
5. Report. Exactly one finding, severity WARNING, or the single line
   `No new comment findings.` when nothing is left.

## Output format

```
WARNING (comments, raised once for this branch): N narrative comments
- path:line  "<comment>"  why: narration | history | dead code | bare ref | restates signature | too long
- ...
Keep only the why, the trap or the coupling, in one short sentence each.
```

Never call this a blocker. Never ask for a re-review of comments. Never
repeat a comment you already reported on this branch.
